title: I Got Rich With Sports Betting When I Applied These 7 Habits
summary: Sports-betting tipster's seven habits: bankroll limits, small units, two-leg slips only, few slips, research, emotional control, withdraw profits; sells a picks Discord while admitting betting usually loses.

assertions.quote: I was able to completely change my life around from making 0 to now making hundreds of thousands of dollars from sports betting

verdicts.note: Bankroll rules limit variance but do not create an edge; sportsbooks and pick'em apps price in a house margin.

The paper does not test any strategy, but documents that the industry's $11B of revenue on $120B wagered implies negative expected returns for the typical bettor and that bookmakers exploit bettors' biases and lack of skill, with bettors' net deposits rising over time.

assertions.quote: I typically Run 1 to 5% of your entire bankroll per slip

verdicts.note: Small stakes reduce ruin risk but cannot overcome negative expected value.

assertions.quote: if the platform wants you to run these high risky plays why do you believe that you should be doing that

verdicts.note: Multi-leg parlays carry far higher hold percentages for operators.

assertions.quote: if you don't secure those profits then guess what eventually it's going to go back to these platforms

verdicts.note: With a house edge, continued play converges to a loss by the law of large numbers.

About 70% of first-time bettors deposit at least twice more and almost 40% over ten times, with quarterly deposits reaching about eight times the initial deposit after 12 quarters, i.e. continued play means continued net money flowing to the books (net deposits are positive in Table A.3).

assertions.quote: just because you landed on heads 10 days in a row does not mean that the 11th day you're going to hit Tails

verdicts.note: Independent events; the gambler's fallacy is well documented.

assertions.quote: if you guys are getting emotional when you're gambling you're doing exactly what these platforms want you to do

verdicts.note: Loss-chasing is the core driver of gambling harm in behavioral research.
Deposits grow substantially over time and the authors attribute part of that growth to addiction and increased tolerance for losses, but loss-chasing itself is not measured.

assertions.quote: if they're losing they are going to force plays they are going to just throw out plays that they're praying to God that hits

verdicts.note: Plausible incentive but no systematic evidence on tipster behavior.
